newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN says inv banking result "fantastic".
newsitem.headline: ABN says inv banking result "fantastic".

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV said on Thursday said its Amsterdam-based investment banking division delivered "fantastic" results in calendar 1996.
Executive board chairman Jan Kalff told a news conference this performance "thwarted" the group trend toward a 50/50 split of profits between Netherlands and the rest of the world.
In a statement, the bank said bonuses grew strongly in line with a 36 percent increase in investment banking business.
It said profit in the Netherlands rose 19.5 percent to 2.70 billion guilders in 1996, or 56 percent of group profit, while profit from abroad increased 32.3 percent to 1.58 billion.
"The profit in the Netherlands is particularly due to the fantastic result in investment banking in Amsterdam," Kalff told reporters.
In the Netherlands, results from financial transactions surged 39.9 percent to 1.02 billion guilders due to strong growth in securities trading and foreign exchange dealing.
The securities trading result rose 39.6 percent to 314 million guilders as equity trading was particularly buoyant.
The foreign exchange dealing result was 31.1 percent higher at 367 million guilders, while the derivatives trading result was almost level with 1995.
